baselines.name: buy_and_hold
baselines.description: long the asset for the whole sample; one entry, one exit, no timing

baselines.name: sma_cross
baselines.description: long while SMA(20) > SMA(50), flat otherwise

baselines.name: volatility_targeted
baselines.description: always long, sized to a 15% annualised volatility target from a 60-bar window

baselines.name: random_entry
baselines.description: 13 seeded random entries held ~12 bars each, matched to the strategy's trade count and duration

baselines.name: always_flat
baselines.description: no positions at any point; the return a strategy must justify

listado.evidence_statement:
In this experiment (BTC-USD 1h 2025-12-12..2026-01-06 (600 bars, seed=20260812)), the configuration produced return=-0.13% sharpe=-8.37 sortino=-2.37 maxDD=0.14% trades=13 win=53.85%. This describes past behaviour on this dataset under these costs and makes no claim about future results. Caveats: only 13 closed trades; too few to separate skill from chance at any confidence worth quoting; the sample covers 25 days, which is unlikely to contain more than one market regime.

Against the mandatory baselines:
  - ahead of buy_and_hold: -0.13% vs -1.57% (maxDD 0.14% vs 4.23%)
  - ahead of sma_cross: -0.13% vs -0.88% (maxDD 0.14% vs 2.83%)
  - ahead of volatility_targeted: -0.13% vs -1.14% (maxDD 0.14% vs 3.54%)
  - ahead of random_entry: -0.13% vs -0.77% (maxDD 0.14% vs 1.95%)
  - not ahead of always_flat: -0.13% vs +0.00% (maxDD 0.14% vs 0.00%)

Verdict: insufficient evidence.
  - 13 closed trades is below the 30 needed to separate skill from chance; no comparison below is conclusive

Past behaviour on one dataset under one cost model. Not a prediction, not a recommendation, and not evidence that the same configuration will behave this way on data it has not seen.
